gen-dafont-ethnocentric-fs-roundo: Fast, wide and a bit aggressive up top, with big bowls under short ascenders. And Roundo keeps the small counters unclogged, so its geometric lowercase stays smooth against all that push.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-atkinson-hype: Ethnocentric spreads its fast, aggressive letters wide apart. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next has big open eyes and unlatched rounds, so a long passage would read approachably and without any clogging.
gen-dafont-ethnocentric-gf-noto-sans-lep: Noto Sans Lepcha reads approachably, its curves keeping a wide opening. Ethnocentric is best at fast, aggressive display with big bowls, while the body font is best at holding a sturdy, cast-iron lowercase.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-bespoke-slab: Bespoke Slab brings grounded, refined serif letters with tall bodies in every lowercase form beneath the heading. Existence is best at industrial, constant-width strokes, while the slab is best at standing tall.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-fira-sans: Existence looks industrial, with wide porthole counters and short-cut terminals. Fira Sans sits beneath with a large x-height and wide-open s curves, so the two read as machined heading and clean, sturdy text.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-gambetta: Existence builds its letters from rods rather than carved blades, with wide porthole counters and terminals cut well short. Gambetta's gently shifting strokes make longer reading feel bookish and graceful.
gen-dafont-existence-fs-supreme: A constant stroke weight with no sparkle, plus porthole counters and short-cut terminals, defines Existence. Supreme gives a crisp, heavy-looking band of text with letters held open, so reading feels steady.
gen-dafont-existence-gf-domine: Dignified is the mood of Domine, with light contrast and breathing room inside each curve. Existence adds a hairline-free a and industrial portholes, so the heading feels machined while the text stays refined.
gen-dafont-exoplanet-fs-public-sans: Public Sans reads trustworthy and hefty, with broad open counters on c and s. And Exoplanet sits above it with tightly shut, sleek letters, so closed shapes meet open ones on the page.
gen-dafont-fenwick-fs-familjen-grotesk: A wire-like monoline skeleton gives Fenwick its graceful, literary look, with bowls that fill the line. And Familjen Grotesk can take a modest size, since its tall lowercase and lively, unfinished bowls stay clear.
